desc:
Custom API development for web and mobile apps gives your website, app or partners a backend they can call safely. Ecom Swift LLC builds the endpoints, connects your database, adds sign-in, tests every route and delivers the code in your own repository.

## What is custom API development?

Custom API development is the building of a backend service that other software can talk to. Your website or mobile app sends a request, such as "get this customer's orders", and the API checks it, reads the database and returns a clean answer. The API sits between your screens and your data.

Building it yourself in a custom way means the endpoints fit your business, instead of bending your business to fit a ready-made tool.

## Why a proper backend matters

A weak backend shows up in small ways first. Screens load slowly, a list returns too much data, an odd input crashes a route, or two apps behave differently because each reads the database its own way. Later these turn into outages and security holes.

A well-made API gives your apps one trusted place for rules. Validation, permissions and business logic live once, instead of being copied into every client. When you add a new app or a partner, they use the same endpoints and get the same behavior.

## How a good API improves your product

Speed and reliability come from details: indexed queries, paging so lists stay small, and clear errors so apps can recover. Automated tests catch mistakes before customers do. Logs show what happened when something goes wrong.

For the business, this means faster feature work and fewer emergencies. A mobile team can build screens against stable endpoints, and a partner can integrate without asking for exceptions. Time saved on firefighting goes back into the product.

## What a production-ready API includes

- Endpoints matching the actions your apps need, built in a language that fits your stack.
- A connection to your database with safe queries.
- Input checks that reject bad data with a clear message.
- Token-based sign-in and permissions on routes that need them.
- Paging, search and filters for lists.
- Automated tests for each route.
- Request logs and usage limits for larger builds.
- Background jobs for slow work such as sending email or building reports.
- Separate staging and live environments, with deployment to your hosting.

## How we build it

We start from your list of data and actions. If you do not have a written design, we sketch the endpoints with you first and agree the shapes of requests and answers. Then we build route by route, testing as we go, and show progress on a staging copy you can try.

At the end the code lives in your repository, runs on your hosting and comes with a short guide and sample calls. The Basic package covers a small set of tested endpoints, Standard adds sign-in, paging and automated tests, and Premium adds logs, limits, background jobs and a handover call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the data and actions in plain words before we begin.
- Keep the code in a repository you own.
- Ask for tests on routes that handle money or personal data.
- Use a staging copy to try changes before they go live.
- Plan hosting and monitoring early.

**Avoid:**
- Putting business rules inside the mobile app only.
- Skipping input checks because the front end already validates.
- Returning every column of a table to every caller.
- Hard-coding secrets in the code.
- Building every possible endpoint on day one.

## Who it is for

A founder with a mobile app prototype who needs a real backend behind it will benefit. A business with a website that must share data with a partner needs endpoints the partner can call. A team that outgrew spreadsheet scripts needs a proper service with sign-in and tests.

## What we need from you

Share a short brief of the data and actions, any screens or wireframes, and your database or hosting details if they exist. We work through a developer or collaborator user in your repository and hosting accounts, so you keep ownership throughout. We never need your passwords. Secrets are stored as environment settings that you control.
